Mandatory fortification of foods with folic acid has caused much controversy, with some advocating this measure as prevention against neural tube defects (below) and others concerned about folic acid supplementation masking vita- min B12 deficiency (above) or having possible carcinogenic ef- fects (above). Epidemiological studies have suggested an asso- ciation between homocysteine and folate concentrations and hearing status. A 3-year controlled study in a country without folic acid food fortification found that supplementation slowed the decline in age-related hearing loss.
